text: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Newcastle. Which public liability lawyers are best?

result.keyword: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Newcastle. Which public liability lawyers are best?
result.markdown:
If you mean **Newcastle, NSW**, there are several credible public-liability specialists. I wouldn’t choose purely on Google reviews; for a shopping-centre slip/fall, I’d prioritise **demonstrated public-liability experience, NSW personal-injury accreditation, and experience dealing with shopping-centre insurers**.

### Firms I’d shortlist

- **Whitelaw McDonald Personal Injury Lawyers - Newcastle** — particularly worth speaking to. Their Newcastle team specifically handles slip-and-fall/public-liability matters, and principal director Matthew Berenger is an **Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury**. The firm says he represented a client injured in a shopping centre in litigation that ultimately went to the High Court. [wmcdlaw.com.au](https://wmcdlaw.com.au/compensation-law/personal-injury-permanent-disability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Burke Mead Lawyers - Newcastle** — a strong local personal-injury practice; its Newcastle team specifically handles public liability, and Emma Mead is listed as an **Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury Law**. [www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au](https://www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au/offices/newcastle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Slater and Gordon Lawyers** — Alexandra Roussos is based in Newcastle and specifically practises in **public liability, premises liability and slips/trips/falls**, among other complex injury matters. [www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/people/alexandra-roussos?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Firths The Compensation Lawyers** — Newcastle-based and specifically advertises slip-and-fall/public-liability claims, with a free claim assessment and no-win-no-fee arrangements. [www.firths.com.au](https://www.firths.com.au/offices/34/newcastle?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **LHD Lawyers Newcastle** — specifically handles public-liability claims involving shopping centres, cafés and other public places. [www.lhd.com.au](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/nsw/newcastle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My first two calls would be Whitelaw McDonald and Burke Mead**, based on the particularly relevant public-liability experience and personal-injury specialist credentials I found. That's a shortlist rather than a guarantee of who will obtain the best result.

### Important: preserve the evidence now

For a shopping-centre fall, **evidence can be crucial**. Keep copies/photos of:

- photos and video of exactly where you fell and the hazard
- the clothing and shoes you were wearing
- your medical records and receipts
- the shopping-centre incident report/reference number
- names/contact details of witnesses
- correspondence from the centre, its insurer, or their lawyers
- CCTV details — **ask the centre in writing to preserve the CCTV footage immediately**, because recordings can be overwritten.

Don't give a detailed statement to the shopping centre's insurer or sign a release before getting legal advice.

NSW public-liability limitation rules can also be complicated, so don't assume you have years to deal with it. [wmcdlaw.com.au](https://wmcdlaw.com.au/compensation-law/personal-injury-permanent-disability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me **which Newcastle shopping centre you fell in (e.g. Westfield Kotara, Charlestown Square, Stockland Green Hills, etc.) and roughly when it happened**, I can also look into **which lawyers have specifically handled shopping-centre/public-liability cases and compare their fees, no-win-no-fee terms, specialist credentials and reviews**.
